<!-- The per-corpus targets run their corpus as testFast's tracks do
       (fastTrack, below: private caches, the same JVM settings), after an
       incremental build. Each starts its own tracks' caches empty and leaves
       the other tracks' and default_repository/caches alone. -->
  <target name ="testCompiler" depends="compileAll"
          description="Test the native code generator: testFast's compiler and othercompiler tracks">
    <mkdir dir="${test.results}"/>
    <mkdir dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <delete quiet="true" dir="${test.caches}/fast-compiler"/>
    <delete quiet="true" dir="${test.caches}/fast-othercompiler"/>
    <parallel threadcount="2">
      <fastTrack id="compiler">
        <include name="**/CompilerJUTest.class"/>
      </fastTrack>
      <fastTrack id="othercompiler">
        <include name="**/OtherCompilerJUTest.class"/>
      </fastTrack>
    </parallel>
    <delete dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <fail message="Tests expected to pass are failing!" if="tests.failed"/>
  </target>

  <target name ="testOtherCompiler" depends="compileAll"
          description="Test the native code generator on other_compiler_tests: testFast's othercompiler track">
    <mkdir dir="${test.results}"/>
    <mkdir dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <delete quiet="true" dir="${test.caches}/fast-othercompiler"/>
    <fastTrack id="othercompiler">
      <include name="**/OtherCompilerJUTest.class"/>
    </fastTrack>
    <delete dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <fail message="Tests expected to pass are failing!" if="tests.failed"/>
  </target>

  <target name ="testLibrary" depends="compileAll"
          description="Test the compiler libraries: testFast's library track">
    <mkdir dir="${test.results}"/>
    <mkdir dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <delete quiet="true" dir="${test.caches}/fast-library"/>
    <fastTrack id="library">
      <include name="**/LibraryJUTest.class"/>
    </fastTrack>
    <delete dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <fail message="Tests expected to pass are failing!" if="tests.failed"/>
  </target>

  <target name ="testOneLibrary" depends="compileAll"
          description="Test the compiled path against the one library: testFast's onelibrary track">
    <mkdir dir="${test.results}"/>
    <mkdir dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <delete quiet="true" dir="${test.caches}/fast-onelibrary"/>
    <fastTrack id="onelibrary" library="one">
      <include name="**/OneLibraryJUTest.class"/>
    </fastTrack>
    <delete dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <fail message="Tests expected to pass are failing!" if="tests.failed"/>
  </target>

  <target name ="testQuick" depends="compileAll"
          description="Test the native code generator: testFast's compiler, othercompiler and library tracks">
    <mkdir dir="${test.results}"/>
    <mkdir dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <delete quiet="true" dir="${test.caches}/fast-compiler"/>
    <delete quiet="true" dir="${test.caches}/fast-othercompiler"/>
    <delete quiet="true" dir="${test.caches}/fast-library"/>
    <parallel threadcount="3">
      <fastTrack id="compiler">
        <include name="**/CompilerJUTest.class"/>
      </fastTrack>
      <fastTrack id="othercompiler">
        <include name="**/OtherCompilerJUTest.class"/>
      </fastTrack>
      <fastTrack id="library">
        <include name="**/LibraryJUTest.class"/>
      </fastTrack>
    </parallel>
    <delete dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <fail message="Tests expected to pass are failing!" if="tests.failed"/>
  </target>

  <!-- One track of the parallel testFast run: a forked JUnit JVM whose
package com.sun.fortress.tests.unit_tests;

import com.sun.fortress.Shell;
import com.sun.fortress.compiler.WellKnownNames;
import com.sun.fortress.repository.ProjectProperties;
import junit.framework.Test;
import junit.framework.TestCase;
import junit.framework.TestSuite;

import java.io.IOException;

/**
 * The .test files of ProjectFortress/one_library_tests, compiled and run against the one
 * library: under FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one, as ant testOneLibrary runs them.  Without the
 * selection the suite is one failing test that says so.
 */
public class OneLibraryJUTest {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        junit.textui.TestRunner.run(suite());
    }

    public static Test suite() throws IOException {
        if (!WellKnownNames.compiledPathUsesOneLibrary) {
            TestSuite unselected = new TestSuite("ProjectFortress/one_library_tests without the one library's selection");
            unselected.addTest(new TestCase("oneLibrarySelected") {
                @Override
                protected void runTest() {
                    fail("one_library_tests runs only where FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one selects the one library, as ant testOneLibrary does");
                }
            });
            return unselected;
        }
        // Make sure there are no compiled files from earlier tests lurking in the
        // repository, unless the harness has already emptied the caches for the run.
        if (ProjectProperties.getBoolean("fortress.junit.reset", true)) {
            Shell.resetRepository();
        }

        String testDir = ProjectProperties.BASEDIR + "one_library_tests";
        boolean failsOnly = !ProjectProperties.getBoolean("fortress.junit.verbose", false);
        TestSuite suite = new TestSuite(
                "Test all .test files in 'ProjectFortress/one_library_tests' against the one library");
        suite.addTest(FileTests.compilerSuite(testDir, true, failsOnly, false));
        return suite;
    }
}

(* A method or getter of either result type, called on a call typed by the intersection of its candidates' return types, or on a variable bound to it, gets the answer of the value's own object. *)
component CoverageReturnMethodCall
export Executable

trait S comprises { U, V } end
trait T comprises { V, W } end
trait U extends S excludes W end
trait M extends { S, T } comprises { V } end
trait V extends M end
trait W extends T end
object Vo extends V end

trait Tagged
  tag(): String = "tagged"
end
trait LeftResult extends Tagged
  getter side(): String = "left side"
  left(): String = "left"
  plusLeft(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = n + 1
  get(n: ZZ32): String = "left at ZZ32"
  pick[\X extends Object\](x: X): X = x
end
trait RightResult extends Tagged
  right(): String = "right"
  get(s: String): String = "right at String"
end
object LeftOnly extends LeftResult end
object RightOnly extends RightResult end
object BothResult extends { LeftResult, RightResult }
  tag(): String = "both"
end

choose(s: S): LeftResult = LeftOnly
choose(t: T): RightResult = RightOnly
choose(v: V): BothResult = BothResult

run(): () = do
  m: M = Vo
  assert(choose(m).left(), "left", "a method of LeftResult on the call")
  assert(choose(m).right(), "right", "a method of RightResult on the call")
  assert(choose(m).side, "left side", "a getter of LeftResult on the call")
  assert(choose(m).plusLeft(41), 42, "a method with an argument on the call")
  assert(choose(m).tag(), "both", "a method that both result types inherit runs the object's own")
  assert(choose(m).get(5), "left at ZZ32", "an overloaded method's declaration in LeftResult")
  assert(choose(m).get("a"), "right at String", "an overloaded method's declaration in RightResult")
  assert(choose(m).pick[\String\]("picked"), "picked", "a generic method of LeftResult on the call")
  r = choose(m)
  assert(r.left(), "left", "a method of LeftResult on a variable bound to the call")
  assert(r.right(), "right", "a method of RightResult on a variable bound to the call")
  assert(r.side, "left side", "a getter of LeftResult on a variable bound to the call")
  println("PASS")
end

end
tests=CoverageReturnMethodCall
compile
link
run

38-
39-An expression consisting of a single subexpression, followed by
40-\KWD{asif}, followed by a type, is a
41-\emph{type assumption}.
42-The value of the expression is the value of the subexpression.
43-The static type of the expression is the given type.
44-The type of the subexpression must be a subtype of the given type.
45-A type assumption considers both the static and the dynamic type of the value
46-of the expression to be the specified type for the purposes of the
47-immediately enclosing function, method, or operator invocation or
48-field access.  This is in contrast to type ascription, which only
49-gives a \emph{static} type to an expression.  Type assumption is used
50-to access a method provided by a supertrait when multiple supertraits
51-provide different methods with the same name.  Fortress thus provides
52-a richer version of type assumption operations such as \texttt{super}
53-in the Java Programming Language.

commit 74f53ec88686cfad27501b649079d471c755b7f0
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   Tue Nov 17 02:48:40 2026 +0000

    The code generator writes each inherited method once into a class and forwards to a body in an api's trait
    
    Climb batch 31, rung M (rows 990, 732 and 571). For a trait's and an
    object's class the code generator gathered the forwarders to inherited
    bodies by a comparison of two domains as schemas over each trait's own
    static parameters, so a generic trait that declared again a method which
    it inherited got the method twice and its class failed as it loaded; and
    it skipped every declaration without a body, an imported api's among
    them, so a body that came through an api's trait that was not first got
    no forwarder and the call died with AbstractMethodError. The class now
    gets each method once, the declaration of the lowest type that declares
    it, compared at the instance that the extends clauses give, and a method
    that an api declares without abstract counts as a body. A functional
    method with self not first is no longer written beside its dispatch
    method. Row 573 is rewritten, and rows 1037 and 1038 are new.
    
    This commit edits the original tree.
    historical: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java
    and ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala.

content.content:
(* A type assumption, e asif T, runs the body that T gives a method or getter, and fixes the declaration that an overloaded call takes (type-annotation.tex, section "Type Assumption"). *)
component AsIfCallsCompiled
export Executable

trait Named
    getter name(): String = "Named"
    greet(s: String): String = "Named greets " || s
    tag(self): String = "Named tag"
    opr PLUS(self, other: Named): String = "Named PLUS"
    pick(x: Named): String = "Named picks Named"
    pick(x: Leaf): String = "Named picks Leaf"
end

trait Titled extends Named
    getter title(): String = "Titled " || self.name
end

object Leaf extends Titled
    getter name(): String = "Leaf"
    greet(s: String): String = "Leaf greets " || s
    tag(self): String = "Leaf tag"
    opr PLUS(self, other: Named): String = "Leaf PLUS"
end

trait Shown[\T extends Object\]
    getter caption(): String = "Shown"
    fcap(self): String = "Shown fcap"
end

trait Listed[\T extends Object\] extends Shown[\T\]
    getter caption(): String = "Listed, " || (self asif Shown[\T\]).caption
end

object Digits extends Listed[\ZZ32\]
    fcap(self): String = "Digits fcap"
end

who(x: Named): String = "Named"
who(x: Leaf): String = "Leaf"

opr ODOT(a: Named, b: Named): String = "Named ODOT Named"
opr ODOT(a: Leaf, b: Leaf): String = "Leaf ODOT Leaf"

caption(x: Named): String = "caption " || x.name

run(): () = do
    assert(Leaf.name, "Leaf", "Leaf's own getter")
    assert((Leaf asif Named).name, "Named", "the getter that Named gives")
    assert(Leaf.greet("you"), "Leaf greets you", "Leaf's own method")
    assert((Leaf asif Named).greet("you"), "Named greets you", "the method that Named gives")
    assert(Leaf.pick(Leaf), "Named picks Leaf", "the overloaded method at Leaf")
    assert((Leaf asif Named).pick(Leaf asif Named), "Named picks Named", "the overloaded method at Named, over two assumptions")
    assert((Leaf asif Titled).name, "Named", "the getter that Titled inherits from Named")
    assert((Leaf asif Titled).title, "Titled Leaf", "Titled's own getter, whose self.name dispatches")
    assert(who(Leaf), "Leaf", "the overload at Leaf")
    assert(who(Leaf asif Named), "Named", "the overload at Named, under the assumption")
    assert(Digits.caption, "Listed, Shown", "a generic trait's getter over self asif its supertrait")
    assert((Digits asif Shown[\ZZ32\]).caption, "Shown", "the getter that a generic supertrait gives")
    assert(tag(Leaf), "Leaf tag", "Leaf's own functional method")
    assert(tag(Leaf asif Named), "Named tag", "the functional method that Named gives")
    assert(fcap(Digits), "Digits fcap", "Digits' own functional method")
    assert(fcap(Digits asif Shown[\ZZ32\]), "Shown fcap", "the functional method that a generic supertrait gives")
    assert(Leaf PLUS Leaf, "Leaf PLUS", "Leaf's own operator method")
    assert((Leaf asif Named) PLUS (Leaf asif Named), "Named PLUS", "the operator method that Named gives, over two assumptions")
    assert(Leaf ODOT Leaf, "Leaf ODOT Leaf", "the operator at two Leafs")
    assert((Leaf asif Named) ODOT (Leaf asif Named), "Named ODOT Named", "the operator at two Nameds, over two assumptions")
    n = Leaf asif Named
    assert(n.name, "Leaf", "a bound assumption is the value, whose getter dispatches")
    assert(who(n), "Leaf", "a bound assumption is the value, whose overload dispatches")
    assert(caption(Leaf asif Named), "caption Leaf", "a function of one declaration takes the value, whose getter dispatches in its body")

content.content:
(* A call of a method that an imported api's trait declares twice, functional or dotted, whose every argument and receiver is a type assumption, runs the body that the assumed types choose (type-annotation.tex, section "Type Assumption"). *)
component AsIfApiTraitCompiled
import AsIfApiTraitApi.{ S, tag }
export Executable

object O extends S end
object P extends S
    tag(self, s: String): String = "p" || s
    m(s: String): String = "p" || s
end

run(): () = do
    k: ZZ32 = 1
    assert(tag(O asif S, "d" asif String), "sd", "tag(O asif S, d asif String)")
    assert(tag(O asif S, k asif ZZ32), "n", "tag(O asif S, k asif ZZ32)")
    assert((O asif S).m("d" asif String), "sd", "(O asif S).m(d asif String)")
    assert((O asif S).m(k asif ZZ32), "n", "(O asif S).m(k asif ZZ32)")
    (* An object's own body at the assumed types does not run: S's does. *)
    assert(tag(P, "d"), "pd", "tag(P, d) runs P's own body")
    assert(tag(P asif S, "d" asif String), "sd", "tag(P asif S, d asif String)")
    assert(P.m("d"), "pd", "P.m(d) runs P's own body")
    assert((P asif S).m("d" asif String), "sd", "(P asif S).m(d asif String)")
    println("PASS")
end

end

#!/bin/bash
# The gate's checker-count stage: run the bytecode compiler's static checker over the
# INTERPRETER's library, with the interpreter's prelude in scope, and print the per-api
# error table, the total and the crash line that follows it.
#
# Why it exists: POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-21, "the library route" - one library, the
# interpreter's, becomes the library the compiler checks - and step 1 of
# coordinator/library-route-judgement.md, which makes the distance to that goal a
# permanent gate stage rather than a one-off script. A change in the count is reported, not red (checker-gate-review.md).
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched:
# javac output and the checker's caches go to the scratch directory (default: $TMPDIR
# or /tmp), and the caches are given to the JVM as -Dfortress.caches, honoured through
# ProjectProperties.java:261-269,283, so default_repository/ is never read or written.
# Exit 0 if the table holds a total; 1 if no table could be produced, or if the table holds
# no total because the run's errors are not the checker's (#stopped, below). 20 s in the
# main tree, measured 2026-09-22; it needs no library rebuild and no warm cache.
#
# The run stops after the type checker (WorldFlip -stop check), since 2026-10-24 (climb batch
# 22): the compiler's own phase order up to and including TYPECHECK, integer literal folding
# included, as the distance stage's DistanceMulti -order check. Past the checker, the code
# generator's refusals are not the checker's errors (FACTS F-34 counts them), and its first
# one throws, so a run on a library the checker passes went on into the code generator and
# printed no total. A run the checker stops runs the same phases as before; a clean check,
# a run that reached the component's check and ended rc 0 with no error line, reads as 0.
#
# The two sources beside this script are copies, taken 2026-09-22 from
# explorations/perf-probes/prelude/, so that the gate does not depend on a probe
# directory: WorldFlip.java (Shell.useInterpreterLibraries() plus
# PhaseOrder.compilerPhaseOrder, both public, which is the world switch without an edit
# to a tracked file; its -stop check added 2026-10-24) and shadow-src/.../StaticChecker.java, a copy of
# ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java with three
# instrumentation points added: it names each compilation unit it checks and prints that
# unit's error count, and it catches the OverloadingChecker crash instead of dying on it.
# It is put AHEAD of ProjectFortress/build on the classpath, the technique of
# perf-probes/prelude/run-all.sh:33-35. A copy of a tracked source goes stale silently,
# so the checksum of the tracked one is recorded here and the table's "#shadow" line
# says whether it still matches.
#
# The overloading checker's memo is off (-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false, read
# at OverloadingChecker.scala:77), since 2026-09-27 (climb batch 7). The memo is keyed on
# declaration pairs and hides 27 to 35 errors depending on the build order once an api's
# overloading check runs (perf-probes/nat/triage.md section 1; FACTS.md, "The hidden
# layer, classified"); with it off every build gives one count. The table's "#cache"
# row says so. On the tree of 2026-09-27 the count is 62 with the memo on and off,
# because the FortressLibrary api stops before its overloading check.
#
# The table, tab-separated, every row tagged:
#   #api        one row per api the checker checked, with that api's error count
#   #total      the errors that the run's last "File X has N errors." line counts, or 0 for
#               a clean check (above)
#   #locations  the distinct file:line those errors were reported at
#   #stopped    in place of #total and #locations, when that line counts errors that the
#               checker did not report: no api's check reported an error and the checker
#               never reached the component, so the library stopped at parse or name
#               binding, before the apis' check or between it and the component's. It names

- Detail: §3.

**Questions for the curator (decisions not taken).**
- Q1: land the walker split as its own rung ahead of row 680's line, or in the same rung?
- Q2: pursue the solver's re-normalization of meets (§2.3), about 95 % of what remains?
  - Ways: a memo of normalized meets shared across analyzers; fewer reductions in `Formula.and`'s fold.
- Q3: make AST hashing independent of identity hashes (row 488)? That would change iteration orders, and so
  message text, once.

**Commands worked out.**
- **JFR, read without the text dump.** A single-file Java program over `jdk.jfr.consumer.RecordingFile`
  aggregates `jdk.ExecutionSample` within an epoch window, by self, inclusive, callers or callees. A frame's
  `getType()` (Interpreted, JIT compiled, Inlined) shows which methods the JVM never compiled.
- **Methods over the limit:** a `java.lang.classfile` scan of `ProjectFortress/build` for `Code` attributes
  longer than 8,000 bytes.
- **The AST generators by hand, in scratch:**
  1. `javac -cp <scala jars>:ProjectFortress/build:ProjectFortress/third_party/astgen/astgen.jar -d <dir>/build ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/astgen/*.java`.
  2. Copy `Fortress.ast` into `<dir>/astgen`.
  3. From there, `java -cp <dir>/build:<scala jars>:ProjectFortress/build:astgen.jar edu.rice.cs.astgen.ASTGen Fortress.ast`. The `.ast` file's `customClassPath ../build` finds the generators.
- **A huge method's compile attempts:** `-XX:-DontCompileHugeMethods -XX:+PrintCompilation`.
- **Moving the identity-hash sequence:** a driver copy that calls `new Object().hashCode()` N times before
  the phases.

# 1. build the driver and the instrumented checker against the tree's own classpath
javac -nowarn -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/classes" \
      "$D/WorldFlip.java" "$D/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java" \
      > "$SCRATCH/javac.txt" 2>&1
if [ $? -ne 0 ] ; then
    echo "checker-count: javac failed; see $SCRATCH/javac.txt" >&2 ; tail -20 "$SCRATCH/javac.txt" >&2 ; exit 1
fi

# 2. run the compiler phase order through the checker over the interpreter's library under a
#    private cache
( cd "$FH" && timeout -k 10 900 java -Xmx4g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches="$SCRATCH/caches" \
       -Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=$OVERLOAD_CACHE \
       -cp "$SCRATCH/classes:$CP" WorldFlip -stop check "$TARGET" ) > "$SCRATCH/run.txt" 2>&1
RC=$?
# A clean check: the checker reached the component, and the run ended rc 0 with no error line.
CLEAN=
if [ "$RC" = 0 ] && grep -q '^@@PROBE checkComponent ' "$SCRATCH/run.txt" && grep -q '^### rc=0$' "$SCRATCH/run.txt" \
   && ! grep -q 'has [0-9]* errors\?\.$' "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ; then
    CLEAN=yes
fi
if [ -z "$CLEAN" ] && ! grep -q 'has [0-9]* errors\?\.$' "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ; then
    echo "checker-count: the run printed no error total (rc=$RC); see $SCRATCH/run.txt" >&2
    tail -20 "$SCRATCH/run.txt" >&2 ; exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv
#
# The run uses a private cache tree so it never touches default_repository/caches
# (fortress.caches system property + FORTRESS_CACHES env; ProjectProperties.java:283,
# same mechanism the suite uses at build.xml:941-943), and a private java.io.tmpdir
# so the 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory of every grammar-importing run (RatsUtil.java:138-144)
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../explorations/experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT="${LADDER_ROOT:-$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp/ladder-r1}"
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT="$FORTRESS_HOME/explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static"
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:7-27

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.
